subtopics.title: What Counts as Non-conventional, and Why South Africa Is Blessed

questions.question: The two properties that rule the whole non-conventional family are:
options: The fuel costs nothing, and the supply is intermittent — the sun keeps office hours and the wind takes unscheduled leave
The fuel is imported, and the supply is constant
The machines are cheap, and the fuel is expensive
The sources are all nuclear-based and steady

questions.question: Non-conventional and renewable are cousins rather than twins because:
options: All renewable sources are conventional
A source can be non-conventional without being a large-scale renewable — like biogas from a feedlot digester
Renewable sources cannot generate electricity
Non-conventional sources all run on fossil fuel

questions.question: The evidence that South Africa's endowment is exceptional includes:
options: Uniform rainfall across all nine provinces
The world's deepest natural harbours
More than two thousand five hundred sunshine hours a year over the interior, world-ranking radiation in the Northern Cape, and dependable winds off two oceans
The largest rivers on the African continent

questions.question: Under REIPPPP, private developers:
options: Receive free land to build coal stations
Buy electricity from the state at fixed prices
Operate the national transmission grid
Compete at auction to build wind and solar plants and sell power on long-term contracts — bidding that drove prices below new coal

subtopics.title: Solar Energy: South African and World Examples

questions.question: The essential difference between PV and CSP is that:
options: PV converts light directly into electricity in semiconductor cells, while CSP concentrates the sun's heat with mirrors to raise steam for a turbine
PV needs water for cooling while CSP needs none
CSP works only on rooftops while PV needs deserts
PV stores heat in molten salt while CSP cannot store anything

questions.question: CSP's trump card over PV is that:
options: It has no moving parts at all
Molten salt held in insulated tanks stays hot for hours, so the plant keeps generating after sunset
Its mirrors work in complete darkness
It produces electricity without any turbine

questions.question: Correctly paired South African solar examples are:
options: PV farms in the Drakensberg and CSP at Richards Bay
CSP plants on the Highveld coalfields
PV farms like Jasper and Droogfontein near Kimberley and De Aar, with CSP at Kathu, Bokpoort and Ilanga in the Northern Cape
A national CSP fleet along the KwaZulu-Natal coast

questions.question: The cheapest solar technology in existence is:
options: The heliostat tower
The rooftop battery inverter
The tracking PV farm
The solar water heater — a panel that warms water directly with no electronics, cutting the geyser's share of the bill

subtopics.title: Wind Energy: South African and World Examples

questions.question: The cube law of wind power says that:
options: Doubling the wind speed multiplies the power by eight, which is why towers climb into faster air
Power falls as the cube of blade length
Three turbines always produce nine times the power of one
Wind farms must be laid out in cubic grids

questions.question: Correctly placed South African wind farms include:
options: Gibson Bay in Gauteng and Sere in Mpumalanga
Gibson Bay, Kouga and Amakhala Emoyeni in the Eastern Cape, Gouda in the Western Cape, and Sere on the west coast
Loeriesfontein on the KwaZulu-Natal coast
Kathu and Bokpoort along the Garden Route

questions.question: Denmark matters in the world wind story because it:
options: Hosts the largest single wind farm on earth
Banned all other forms of generation
Pioneered the industry, draws roughly half its electricity from wind, and exports its turbine technology worldwide
Was the first country to build offshore coal stations

questions.question: Wind's cost column includes:
options: Heavy water consumption and ash disposal
Carbon dioxide emissions during operation
Expensive daily fuel deliveries
Intermittency, neighbours' objections over sight and sound, bird and bat collisions demanding careful siting, and the need for backup in still air

subtopics.title: The Future: Economy, Environment and the Honest Obstacles

questions.question: The positive economic effects of non-conventional energy in South Africa include:
options: The cheapest new electricity available, hundreds of billions in private investment, rural jobs and community trusts in bypassed districts, and a green manufacturing ladder
Guaranteed employment for all coal miners
The immediate end of all electricity tariffs
Free electricity for the Northern Cape

questions.question: The negative economic effect that the phrase just transition addresses is that:
options: Renewable plants pay no taxes
Coal supports around ninety thousand concentrated mining jobs while finished renewable plants employ small crews, usually in other provinces — shifting work between regions and skills
Wind farms raise the price of wool
Solar farms prevent all other land uses forever

questions.question: Environmentally, non-conventional energy measured against the coal baseline offers:
options: No gains — the footprints cancel out
Lower costs but heavier water use
No carbon dioxide, no sulphur dioxide or smog, and close to zero water use — against honest debits in land, birds and bats, and panel and blade disposal
Zero impacts of any kind whatsoever

questions.question: The three obstacles that will set the pace of South Africa's transition are:
options: Sunshine, wind speed and rainfall
Uranium supply, oil prices and exchange rates
Panel imports, port capacity and road quality
The saturated grid between the Cape provinces and Gauteng, intermittency managed by the mix, and policy certainty in the auction rounds

subtopics.title: Fuel That Falls From the Sky

questions.question: The free filling station image captures the fact that:
options: Sunshine and wind cost nothing — only the catching machinery costs money, unlike coal which must be dug, railed and burned every day
Renewable plants give away free petrol
Wind farms refuel passing vehicles
Solar panels never need to be paid for

questions.question: The five words that hold the whole modern energy argument are:
options: Burn more coal more cheaply
Free but moody, costly but steady
Sun and wind beat everything
Storage answers every possible question

questions.question: Germany's role in the endowment argument is to show that:
options: Cloudy countries cannot use solar power
Only rich countries may join REIPPPP
A grey-skied country became a solar superpower on about half South Africa's sunshine — so our race is about pumps, not fuel
European sunshine is stronger than African sunshine

questions.question: The PV panel's one-line secret is that it:
options: Converts light straight into current with no moving parts — silent as glass, strongest at noon, asleep by nightfall
Spins a hidden turbine using warm air
Boils water inside the panel to make steam
Stores sunlight chemically for later use

questions.question: CSP's building-sized thermos means that:
options: The mirrors are kept warm overnight
Insulated tanks of molten salt stay hot for hours — Bokpoort banks roughly nine hours — so supper-time electricity is brewed from lunchtime sun
The plant stores cold water for the turbines
The receiver tower doubles as a water tank

questions.question: Wind turbines share their land comfortably because:
options: The blades never turn during daylight
The towers are invisible from ground level
Sheep graze on the veld between the towers while farmers bank rent and communities hold a revenue share
Each turbine is fenced off with its own dam

questions.question: The world name-drops for a solar and wind essay are:
options: Brazil for wind, Canada for CSP, Japan for coal
Russia for panels, India for mirrors, Egypt for turbines
Australia for storage, Kenya for offshore wind
China builds and hosts the most of nearly everything, Denmark runs about half its country on wind, and Spain proved molten salt could carry the night

subtopics.title: The Relay Race and the Baton

questions.question: Fumble one — the extension cord — refers to:
options: The saturated transmission lines between the Cape provinces' sun and wind and Gauteng's demand, making thousands of kilometres of new wire the true bottleneck
Faulty wiring inside wind turbine towers
Households using too many extension leads
The distance between Koeberg and Cape Town

questions.question: The night shift is covered by a mix in which:
options: Coal stations switch on only after midnight
CSP salt and batteries store, pumped storage shifts energy across the hours, and coastal wind often blows while solar sleeps
Solar panels run on moonlight at reduced power
Factories are forbidden from working at night

questions.question: Passing the baton justly to protect the coal towns means:
options: Keeping every coal station open indefinitely
Moving all miners to the Northern Cape immediately
Scheduled retraining, pensions and replacement industry for coal country, financed partly by international transition packages
Banning renewable plants in Mpumalanga

questions.question: The finish-line verdict on South Africa's non-conventional future is that:
options: The direction is still entirely undecided
The resource is too weak to matter
Coal will regain its cost advantage soon
The direction is settled and only the speed is argued — and speed hangs on wires, storage and justice
